paragraphs.text: An exhortation to repentance, Zep 2:1-3. The judgment of the Philistines, Zep 2:4-7 of Moab and Ammon, Zep 2:8-11\, of Ethiopia, Zep 2:12, and Assyria, Zep 2:13-15.
call a solemn assembly, as Joe 1:14, proclaim a fast. Let all have notice given to meet on this work, and, being gathered together, search yourselves, your hearts and ways, and repent.
repeated to affect them the more, and to hasten them to it, and make them serious in it.
of the Jews, yet a people, yet my people, though next door almost to being no people.

neither desirous to return, nor desirable in your return; foolishly unwilling to return, and utterly unworthy to be received on your return: yet gather together, search your ways, and try what you may do for your safety.

the Word of the prophet which declares the purpose of God against this sinful people, bring forth: the degree is pregnant, nay, hath gone a great while, but is now like a woman near her full time, ready to bring forth: be you speedy in your repentance, lest your miseries break forth of the womb of Divine vengeance and destroy you. Before the day, the day of your calamities, Babylon’s rage, and God’s just displeasure,
carry you away as the wind carrieth chaff away for the fire, while the good grain is gathered and preserved.

the heat of anger. It was jealousy like fire, Zep 1:18, and here it is the heat of that fire, intimating the greatness of the anger. Come upon you; as a storm from on high, with violence irresistible and destructive; and the warning is doubled to make them take it.
turn to him with sound and true repentance, pray for pardon, engage in new obedience, inquire in the law what is your duty, and do it; fear, worship, depend on the Lord alone.
ye humble ones, who have not hardened yourselves with the stubborn, proud, idolatrous hypocrites, but have trembled at the word of the Lord.
of Judea, which is here spoken of, as Zep 1:2.
obeyed his precepts; so doth the Scripture express obedience to the law of God by doing judgment, Deu 4:5 Psa 119:121.
inquire and know the righteousness which God commandeth, which you ought to persist in, and continue ye in it.
carry it humbly towards God, and patiently under his corrections; so wait on the just and merciful God.
this is sufficient to raise hope; if it be not sure, if it be hard, yet it is not impossible.
under the wing of Divine protecting Providence kept safe from, or in, these troubles they shall be either averted or abated.
it is time to seek some refuge, high time to seek it in God, for your neighbours, as well as you, shall be destroyed, there shall he no refuge for you among your neighbours.
a chief city of the Philistines, very strong by its situation, and by art fortified; a frontier toward Egypt, and not full three miles from the sea.
when the conquering army of the Chaldeans shall come against it, shall be forsaken either by the flight or captivity of the inhabitants.
another of the strong cities of the Philistines, which fell to the tribe of Dan, and was a maritime town.
utterly wasted, so the abstract doth imply.
Babylonians: see Eze 25:15-17.
into captivity, cast them out of their own and force them into a strange land. Ashdod; a strong fortified city of Palestina, called in aftertimes Azotus.
it shall be taken by force at noon, or the citizens led away captive in the heat of the day, and under parching heats.
famous for its infamous idolatry, where Baalzebub was worshipped, the chief seat of devil-worship.
utterly extirpated, no more to spring up: see
Jer 47:4,5: it shall be as a tree pulled up by the roots; or maimed, as horses that are houghed, as Jos 11:9.
now all the Philistines are threatened, whereas before he named only those four cities.
the coasts of the great or western sea, now the Mediterranean, on which the Philistines of old did dwell.

or destroyers, men that were stout, but fierce, and perhaps terrible to neighbours and foreigners that had the hard hap to be forced on their coasts by violence of sea. They were great soldiers, and lived Switzerlike, guards to David, it may be to other kings also.
his purpose, his threats too by his prophet.
that part that the Philistines did by three keep from the Jews.
though the Chaldeans be the men that shall destroy, yet the Lord will do it also; they his servants, he chief, in doing it.
no more cities, nor citizens to dwell therein.
This confirms the former, tells us what shall be in those parts; instead of cities full of rich citizens, there shall be cottages for shepherds watching over their flocks.
the sea-coast, the land of the Philistines,
either that escaped, as some did, or else survived the captivity;
the two tribes, one named, both included.
their Rocks.
in places where houses of Ashkelon formerly stood,
both shepherds and flocks too.
paragraphs.anchor: shall they lie down in the evening

paragraphs.text: the everlasting Jehovah,
from their fathers by covenant,
in mercy remembering his covenant with them,
or shall send to receive their prisoners or captives; or return their captivity, and by the command of Cyrus give them liberty of returning into their own country.

either the prophet for himself, or for the people, speaks this; or else, more likely, in the name of God, assures the Jews that God had heard, observed, resented, and was highly displeased with that he heard.

a people of near kin to the Jews, born of Lot’s daughter, seated eastward of Canaan, upon the Dead Sea and Jordan, a powerful people, and as proud; whose pride broke out on all occasions against the Jews, as appears from first to last: Isa 16:6, and Jer 48:29,30, brand them as very proud.
a people as near as Moab to Jewish blood, and as bitter against them, Neh 4:2,3, bitter scoffers and jeerers.

invading their frontiers, and spoiling them with insolence.
the most solemn oath, fit for none but God himself to use: see Eze 14:16.
who have all things at my disposal, and can arm all creatures against these proud revilers.
who by covenant am Israel’s God, and Israel is my people, in whose reproaches I am reproached.

this is a proverbial speech in Scripture phrase to speak great destruction, as Isa 1:9. Moab and Ammon were not destroyed by fire, as Sodom and Gomorrah; but the next words are an explication of these.
not cultivated, but run over with nettles, as if it were only to breed them.
a salt, dry, barren earth, fit only to dig salt out of.
never more to be manured and inhabited, or not for a long, a very long time.
either the few left with Gedaliah, or the remnant that returned out of Babylon.
provoked by the injuries of Moab and Ammon, shall take arms, overcome, and spoil them.
settle upon their lands, and dwell in those parts that are fit for habitation.
this grievous ruin like Sodom’s, this just retaliation; they insulted over Israel, Israel shall tread on them.
haughty mind and carriage: see Zep 2:8.
defamed, spoken lies and scandals against the Jews, lessening them.
their persons and exploits.
against the only people of the Lord of hosts, who suffered reproach with his people and in them, for Moabites and Ammonites, as others, boasted of their gods above the true God:
paragraphs.anchor: Against the people of the Lord of hosts

paragraphs.text: or, the Lord, who is to be feared, is against or above them, and will make it appear that he is terrible in his doings.
Moabites and Ammonites, and their gods, of whom they gloried.

starve; though now their altars are filled with sacrifices, and their bowls run over, as if they designed to make their gods fat; but they shall want their sacrifices and drink offerings, these shall be few or quite cease, and their priests grow lean. There shall be a consumption among them all.
idols, heathen gods,
of those lands, Dagon, Chemosh, Molech, &c., that are gods no where else but on earth, and among the deceived; or gods of the earth., as sons of the earth, vile, spurious gods.
men of that country whose gods are undone, or all men, shall know, own, and worship the God of Israel.
where he dwelleth, not only at Jerusalem, or in this mount, but every where.
either literally, as we now see it fulfilled, or as the Jews interpret isles to be transmarine places. So they wait for his law, as foretold Isa 42:4.
of all nations in all parts of the world. This is eminently fulfilled by the prevailing of the gospel.

The prophet doth not speak of the African Ethiopians, south of Egypt, but of the Arabian Ethiopians, much nearer to Canaan, whose country was called Cusaea, with the addition Ethiopia Cusaea. See Hab 3:7.
punished by war, and your people cut off,
Nebuchadnezzar and his Chaldeans, called here God’s sword, for God employed and prospered them.
the Lord God of Israel, or the Chaldean monarch as God’s servant herein,
engage all his power, and use it to the utmost, against the north, i.e. as follows, Assyria, which lay northward of Judea, but more due north from Babylon, if I mistake not.
overthrow that great and ancient kingdom of Assyria. of which more at large in Nahum. Nineveh; chief city of that kingdom. See Nah 1:1. A desolation; most desolate, Nah 3:10-12.
will turn those well-watered places into dry, thirsty, and barren land, as a wilderness.
Nineveh shall be so razed that flocks of cattle shall lie down in the midst of it, as before of the Philistines, Zep 2:6.
all sorts of beasts which are found in those countries, the tame under the girard of watching shepherds, and wild ones seeking their prey, will attend about those places.
paragraphs.anchor: All the beasts of the nations

paragraphs.text: birds that are solitary, and delight in desolate places, in reedy fens, where they seek their food, and are looked on as unlucky birds.
shall either make their nests there, or seek and choose their lodging there; they shall roost there in the night upon the pillars, or turrets, or pinnacles.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall lodge in the upper lintels

paragraphs.text: these doleful creatures shall make a more doleful noise, that shall be all the music to be heard in their desolate windows.
paragraphs.anchor: Their voice shall sing in the windows

paragraphs.text: the lowest part of their houses; from top to bottom nothing but wastes and ruin; instead of beautiful ladies looking out at windows and doors and singing, now cormorants and bitterns, and their doleful notes.
paragraphs.anchor: Desolation shall be in the thresholds

paragraphs.text: or, when the Babylonian hath burnt the houses, or beat down the curious roofs and coverings of cedar, the beauty and the defence of their houses.
paragraphs.anchor: For he shall uncover the cedar work

paragraphs.text: we may suppose the prophet, or the Jews, or all passengers, standing still and wondering, nay, upbraiding Nineveh, all mirth and jollity once, but now all sorrow and grief.
in so great confidence and security, as if it had been impossible she should ever have fallen from her glory.
persuaded herself into an opinion very ill becoming any but God himself.
none that can contend with me, that will be so hardy as to attempt against me, none able to overthrow me. Somewhat like Tyre, Eze 28:12, &o.

she thought none was like her in glory, power, and wealth. now there is none like her indeed, but it is for misery and desolations. It may be either the speech of one that laments and wonders at it, or of one that rejoiceth at it.
paragraphs.anchor: How is she become a desolation!

paragraphs.text: where palaces for princes stood, now are places for beasts; where nobles dwelt, now do ignoble cattle couch.
paragraphs.anchor: A place for beasts to lie down in

paragraphs.text: deride their arrogancy, and condemn their ungodly pride and security, yet with some pity toward this desolate city.
